captured_via: Cat Footwear organic search (Salesforce Commerce Cloud / SFRA), server-side fetch of /US/en/search?q= — product names from tile image alt text; Einstein recommendations (JS-only) excluded, so results are organic. Category-matching queries redirect to the category page; known-item queries redirect to the product page (counted as a direct hit). 1186 product judgments across 245 terms.
headline: Cat Footwear search across 245 terms answers 78% (53 terms return nothing). It is strong where a shopper types the catalog language: model/known-item lookups (100% coverage) and attribute queries (93% - steel toe, waterproof, leather) return relevant results, and a model name like diagnostic jumps straight to the exact boot. The weakness is RECALL on compositional queries: job-function/use-case searches have only 60% coverage (boots for welding, nurses, logging return zero) and intent 67% - despite Cat stocking suitable products. Two root causes: (1) the engine needs exact category words (6 inch boots -> 0 but 6 inch work boots works; lace up boots -> 0 but lace up work boots works); (2) it does not parse natural-language use-cases into attributes. Some zeros are genuine assortment gaps (sandals, flip flops, dress shoes - Cat does not make them), which is merchandising, not search.
verdict: Strong on models (100% coverage) and attributes (93%); the gap is recall on compositional queries - 40% of use-case searches and ~30% of synonym/intent searches return zero, a mix of real search bugs (lace up boots, 6 inch boots) and true assortment gaps (sandals, flip flops).

findings.title: Compositional use-case queries return ZERO despite matching stock
findings.detail: Job-function coverage is only 60% (20 of 50 return nothing): boots-for-welding, boots-for-nurses, boots-for-logging, boots-for-masonry, shoes-for-restaurant-work all -> 0, though Cat stocks suitable work boots/shoes. Intent coverage 67%. The engine does not parse multi-word natural-language queries into attributes/use-cases. Fix candidate: query understanding + use-case-to-attribute mapping.

findings.title: Search needs the exact category words - near-misses return zero
findings.detail: 6-inch-boots -> 0 but 6-inch-WORK-boots -> results; lace-up-boots -> 0 but lace-up-work-boots -> results; trail-shoes -> 0 though Cat stocks hikers. The engine requires exact catalog tokens and does not generalize/stem. Fix candidate: broaden category synonyms and stemming so partial phrasings resolve.

findings.title: Separate search misses from true assortment gaps among zero-result synonyms
findings.detail: Of 13 synonym zeros, most are ASSORTMENT gaps (Cat makes none): sandals, flip flops, dress shoes, clogs, mules, slides, boat shoes, deck shoes, moccasins, trainers, tennis/running shoes -> merchandising, not search. But a few are search/nav gaps (lace up boots, kids shoes). Classify each before prioritizing a fix. Synonym coverage 71%.

findings.title: Known-item and attribute search are excellent
findings.detail: Literal/model queries: 100% coverage, grade ~2.35 (best dataset) - model names route straight to the product page (diagnostic, exposition, alloy toe boots -> exact PDP). Attribute queries: 93% coverage - steel toe, waterproof, composite toe, leather all strong. The engine is well-tuned for its focused catalog when queried in catalog terms.

findings.title: Recall-style engine - rank by coverage x demand and classify each zero
findings.detail: Cat Footwear returns nothing on a miss (78% overall coverage; 53 zero-result terms), unlike big-box engines that answer everything shallowly. Weight zero-result rate x Google demand and classify each zero as search-bug vs assortment-gap (catalog guardrail), not grade alone. (Grades still finalizing at time of writing.)
